title: Reciprocal and Radical Composition Analysis
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Let f(x) = 1/x and g(x) = 1 + sqrt(x). Find formulas and natural domains for (f o g)(x) and (g o f)(x).

steps.title: Evaluate (f o g)(x) and Its Domain
steps.explanation: Inner function g requires x >= 0. The outer function f requires its denominator 1 + sqrt(x) != 0. Since sqrt(x) >= 0 for all x >= 0, 1 + sqrt(x) >= 1 > 0, so the denominator is never zero on [0, inf).
steps.why: A sum of 1 and a non-negative real radical is strictly positive, creating no real zeroes.

steps.title: Evaluate (g o f)(x) and Its Domain
steps.explanation: Inner function f requires x != 0. The outer function g requires its radicand 1/x >= 0. The fraction 1/x is non-negative and defined precisely when x > 0.
steps.why: The quotient of positive numerator 1 and variable x is positive if and only if x is positive.

steps.title: Summarize the Distinct Domains
steps.explanation: Notice the boundary behavior: x = 0 is included in D(f o g) because g(0) = 1 and f(1) = 1, but x = 0 is strictly excluded from D(g o f) due to division by zero in f.
steps.why: Boundary inclusion depends strictly on whether the inner function evaluates safely at the endpoint.
